title: 4D Debug Log Analyzer
author: Josh Fletcher, Technical Services Team Member, 4D Inc.
featured_technology: 4D Debug Log (4DDL) file / SET DATABASE PARAMETER
Sample 4D database (Design Mode) with import/reporting engine
DBL_ prefixed API (DBL_M_Import, DBL_M_LogSummary, DBL_DATA_DenormalizeData, DBL_DATA_CalcExecTimes, DBL_RPT_ commands)
Tab-delimited text export for spreadsheet analysis

historical_commentary.text: This note provides a sample 4D database that parses the 4DDL debug log (interpreted-mode only) into a relational [Debug_Logs]/[Log_Lines] schema so developers can generate per-method call-count and execution-time statistics -- a genuinely clever use of 4D itself to analyze 4D's own logging output at a time when spreadsheets couldn't handle millions of log lines. The core technique (parsing a text log into tables, then reporting) is timeless and the underlying 4DDL log format is still part of 4D today, but the tool itself is a Design Mode-era binary database (not a modern Project mode component) and predates 4D's built-in performance analysis tools; a developer today would more likely reach for 4D's integrated Debugger/Runtime Explorer, structured logging, or a dedicated APM-style solution rather than hand-rolling a log-import database. The note is explicit that it only handles interpreted-mode logs, a limitation that still applies.
related_updates: 4D's built-in Debugger and code coverage/profiling tools have expanded significantly since v11
Project mode (4D v17+, 2018) means a modern equivalent tool would ship as a text-based .4DProject rather than a binary database
